newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar announces two new gas finds.
newsitem.headline: Qatar announces two new gas finds.

text.p: Qatar, which sits on top of the world's third largest reserves of gas, said on Tuesday it had discovered two more deposits of natural gas.
"Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) has discovered two gas reservoirs in the southern culmination of the onshore Dukhan field", a QGPC press statement said.
Dukhan, which gave Qatar its first barrel of oil in 1949, supplies all of Qatar's onshore crude from reserves which are estimated at around two billion barrels.
The new gas finds in the Diyab sector of the Dukhan field were of "modest size when compared with current proven gas reserves of the country," QGPC said.

Qatar's proven gas reserves, mostly located in its offshore continental shelf -- called North Field -- are the centrepiece of the Gulf Arab state's multi-billion dollar liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects.
The Diyab reservoirs were discovered at a depth of 11,500 feet into the Khuff formation.
The discovery well tested 14 million cubic feet of gas a day and 2,000 barrels a day of condensate through a 64/64-inch choke with 1050 psi (pressure per second inch).
QGPC said additional appraisal wells would be required to firm up the size of the accumulations and possible future development.
Qatar's gas reserves stand at 530 trillion cubic feet.
